summary:
Technical re-review of phase:f-compensation, iteration 2 (sub-mv46nmw5-019e21c8, responding to rev-mv45ljos-01f00a5d; f2 reset handoff ho-mv46cije-013aeaff, commit 66206c9; tree 57221f73). All 61 artifacts match the submission.

**Tree note.** Rework-6 (FU-33 and FU-46, test-only, under its own gate) changed test/api/uploads-retention.test.js and test/timing/planner-sec-b1.test.js during this review; no phase F artifact changed. Every check I cite was re-run on the settled tree 622af87f. The security draft phase-f-security-2.md (FINAL, verdict APPROVE) is folded in.

**Code change since iteration 1.** Exactly three f2 files changed:
- saga.js: holdOperation, +28/-1;
- capture-compensation.test.js: +157/-1;
- admin-reset.test.js: +20/-4.

**Plan commands, re-run on the new tree.**
- f1: 40/40 (ev:ev-mv47mhi3-0110ea23).
- f2: 59/59 (ev:ev-mv47mtlx-01c8a38e).
- f3: 205/205 (ev:ev-mv47miet-01c9d09a).
- f4 under the suite lock, green on the first run: npm test 2270 tests, 2262 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped; NFR5 p95 58.4 ms; browser 14/14 (ev:ev-mv47tl1n-016af5d0).

**TR-F-1 is resolved; I verified it with my own probe.** The FU-49 probe, with the resolution's expectations (ev:ev-mv47n3s8-015a5cc7), shows:
- epochs 2,2,...,2 over 8 ticks, one read per tick, 0 sends;
- `failed_needs_attention` from tick 7 (17.5 min after the original timeout; the clock was not restarted);
- after recovery, `executed` with one capture per authorization.

The same probe fails on the iteration-1 tree with epochs 2..10 (control ev:ev-mv47n4y0-0138cad2).

**Mutants against the fixes.** I ran 5, in fresh directories with diffs kept (ev:ev-mv47pa98-0198bb63; sources ev:ev-mv47pe61-0123e309). All 5 are killed by assertions:
- the hold reverted;
- the unknown clock restarted;
- the fence removed;
- MB, now killed by an f2 file (SEC-F-1);
- the unbounded pass, which now fails in 17 s instead of hanging (TR-F-2).

**Security agrees.** P-HOLD G1-G5 (ev:ev-mv46u1oo-0168894e) finds no stale-holder write, no backward move from a newer state, and no lost update between restore and hold. Across 20 random-failure seeds there is exactly one capture per authorization.

**Other findings.**
- TR-F-3 is resolved: the labels and the RISK-18 title are corrected, and FU-52 is routed.
- The info items are routed to FU-52..59 with owners. Decisions dec-mv46ovf2-017bf12d and dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af apply, and FU-33 is in rework-6 now.
- New info: TR-F2-1, which merges SEC-F2-I1 (under flapping reads the epoch is bounded by successful reads, not constant), and SEC-F2-C, security's three conditions on the later backend rework.

Decision: approve.

findings.title: (merges SEC-F2-I1) Under flapping reads the epoch is bounded by successful reconciler reads, not constant; the plan still escalates
findings.detail:
**What still happens.** holdOperation returns the operation to `unknown` after each failed holder read. If, on the next tick, the reconciler's own read succeeds (CREATED), the operation is restored, taken over (epoch + 1) and held again. Security's G5 (ev:ev-mv46u1oo-0168894e) shows epochs up to 7 within 12 random-failure ticks for some seeds; most stay at 2.

**Why it is acceptable.**
- Every takeover is backed by a fresh CREATED read.
- No send happens without a holder read showing CREATED, and no seed doubled a capture.
- The operation reads `unknown` between ticks with the ORIGINAL unknown_since, so row 2 escalates after RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN. MG2 confirms that the clock is not restarted.
- The persistent-outage case keeps the epoch constant (my probe v2).
findings.recommendation: No change required. Owner: delivery-lead (verification report, item 21). Resolved when item 21 states that the epoch grows only with successful reconciler reads, and that a flapping provider still escalates through row 2.

findings.title: (security) Three conditions on the backend rework that dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af opens after phase F approval
findings.detail:
1. **FU-59 / SEC-F-I7:** the handover block must apply per order, not per plan. handoverAllowed (orders.js L51-L62) checks every operation of the plan, so adding `refunded` to HANDOVER_BLOCKING_PAYMENT as written would also block the sibling orders of a partially refunded plan, contrary to spec revision 2 row 7 / OQ-D2.
2. **FU-58 / SEC-F-I6:** the supplier route's checkRefusalReason itself must refuse or strip bidi overrides (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069), or the server must isolate the reason when it composes the message.
3. **FU-54 / SEC-F-I1:** `owedRefund` must be true exactly for `captured` with cancel_requested_at set. Each stranded entry also carries `planStatus`, and the fake-provider wording must not mention the Sandbox dashboard.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
**Fix.** saga.js holdOperation (L547, called at L617) puts a held operation back to `unknown` with the original unknown_since, under the epoch fence.

**Condition (a), the stuck state escalates.** Met. My probe v2 on the new tree: `failed_needs_attention` from tick 7 (17.5 min after the timeout).

**Condition (b), the epoch is settled.** Met by the code, so no decision is needed. Epochs are 2,2,...,2 over 8 ticks, with one read per tick and 0 sends; after recovery the plan is `executed` with one capture per authorization (ev:ev-mv47n3s8-015a5cc7).

**Discrimination.** The same probe fails on the iteration-1 tree with epochs 2..10 (control ev:ev-mv47n4y0-0138cad2).

**Tests.** The new tests (capture-compensation L563 and the stale-holder test at L632) kill all three of my mutants of the fix: hold reverted, clock restarted, fence removed (ev:ev-mv47pa98-0198bb63).

**Security.** P-HOLD G1-G5 (ev:ev-mv46u1oo-0168894e) agrees.

**Regression.** The full suite passes under the lock (ev:ev-mv47tl1n-016af5d0).
